name: Hutter Prize (enwik9 / enwik8) rules and record
version: Baseline shipped: a simple order-N context-mixing or PPM-style byte compressor (we write it) plus xz/zstd numbers on a 10-100 MB Wikipedia-XML slice; scored as compressed size + decoder size -> Reference: paq8hp12any / lstm-compress / cmix-class model (see LTCB row for sizes); record page: fx2-cmix-T 100,424,672 B on enwik9
licence: Rules: submissions must be OSI-approved open source before payout; enwik9 data licence NOT stated on the pages (not found)
surface: compressed bytes (archive + decompressor) lower is better; bits/byte. Score = (baseline_size - size)/(baseline_size - ref_size)
reference: Reference: paq8hp12any / lstm-compress / cmix-class model (see LTCB row for sizes); record page: fx2-cmix-T 100,424,672 B on enwik9
notes: OVERLAP: close to public 'write-compressor' subject, flag. q:"Must run in ≲50 hours using a single CPU core and <10GB RAM and <100GB HDD on our test machine." Record 100,424,672 B Vladimir Ivanov 24 Jul 2026 (index page). Rules: no GPU, 10GB RAM, time 70000/T hours (Geekbench5 T). OOD hidden split idea: ship enwik-like slice, hide a different-domain text (other-language Wikipedia XML, source code, forum text) of 5-10 MB so dictionary/tuning on enwik fails. INFERRED run time per eval: paq8hp-class ~38 us/B so 10 MB hidden file ~6-7 min compress + same decompress on 1 core; cmix-class ~0.6 ms/B = ~100 min per 10 MB so too slow. Levers: model mix (orders 1-6, match, word model), preprocessing/dictionary, SSE/APM, counter-state tuning, hashing/memory layout.

notes: Notebook q:"Data from the OR3 benchmark, containing 20 bin packing instances each with 500 items." Weibull 5k: 5 instances x 5,000 items, capacity 100; OR3 capacity 150. OOD split: tune on Weibull-like or OR1-OR2 style, hidden on different Weibull shape/scale, n=10k-100k, or triplet class (binpack5-8, cap 100). Weakness: single lever (one priority function), tiny eval; to make multi-lever extend to vector/2D bin packing or add offline repacking + lookahead. INFERRED: ~2-10 s per eval (pure-Python loop over items with numpy over bins). Notes: FunSearch paper (nature.com) paywalled/redirected, not opened. Overlap: well-known public task.
